items.title: Fused MoE RoutingMethodType has no sqrtsoftplus scoring — DeepSeek-V4.1 cannot use the internal-routing trtllm path
items.body:
## Summary

`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` computes routing inside the kernel, selected from a fixed `RoutingMethodType` enum. All ten current methods score with **softmax**, **sigmoid**, or plain **top-k**:

| # | method | scoring |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Default | Softmax -> TopK |
| 1 | Renormalize | TopK -> Softmax |
| 2 | DeepSeekV3 | Sigmoid -> BiasAdd -> Top2-in-group -> Top4 groups -> TopK |
| 3 | Llama4 | Top1 -> Sigmoid |
| 4 | RenormalizeNaive | Softmax -> TopK -> Renormalize |
| 5 | TopK | TopK only |
| 6 | SigmoidRenorm | Sigmoid -> TopK -> Renormalize |
| 7 | MiniMax2 | Sigmoid+Bias -> TopK -> ScaledSumNormalize |
| 8 | Sigmoid | Sigmoid -> TopK |
| 9 | TopKSigmoid | TopK -> Sigmoid |

**DeepSeek-V4.1 scores with `sqrtsoftplus`**, which is none of these.

## Why this matters

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (`config.json`, `text_config`):

```
scoring_func          = sqrtsoftplus
topk_method           = noaux_tc
n_routed_experts      = 384
num_experts_per_tok   = 6
n_group               = None
topk_group            = None
routed_scaling_factor = 1.5
norm_topk_prob        = True
```

Because no enum value reproduces this, the model can only use `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, supplying pre-computed expert assignments. Selecting a different `RoutingMethodType` anyway would not be a workaround — it would silently select **different experts**, i.e. a correctness bug rather than a config mismatch.

In practice the first symptom is misleading. SGLang passes `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3` for this family, so users see:

```
trtllm_fused_moe_runner.cu:155
FLASHINFER_CHECK(topkGroup <= 4, "For DeepSeek routing method, must have topkGroup <= 4")
```

which reads like a grouping/config problem, when the actual blocker is the unsupported scoring function.

## Request

Either:

1. add a `sqrtsoftplus` routing method (softplus-then-sqrt scoring, ungrouped top-k with correction bias and renormalization), or
2. document that models whose scoring is outside the enum must use the routed variant — and note the consequence, that they lose deferred finalize (see the companion issue filed against SGLang).

Even just (2) would save people the misdiagnosis: the `topkGroup` error points at the wrong thing.

## Environment

- FlashInfer 0.6.18, SGLang `feat/decode-first-on-dsv41` @ a70d0d46
- 4x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0
- `AtomicChat/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4-nvidia`, TP4

items.title: H100 CI broken on main since #5131: cudnn-frontend 1.28 vs backend 9.24 rejects non-ragged Stats layout (134 nodes, blocks all PRs)
items.body:
`JIT Unittest (H100)` has been failing on `main` since [#5131](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5131) raised the `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` floor to 1.28.0. Because `Test Results Summary` is a required status check, this currently blocks **every** PR from merging, not just the ones touching attention.

Filing rather than fixing since the remedy is a dependency-policy call that belongs to the author of #5131 (@Anerudhan).

## Symptom

134 failed nodes on H100, all in two files:

| file | nodes | error |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill_token_indptr.py` | 133 | `cudnnGraphNotSupportedError: For cuDNN version below 9.26.0, a non-ragged Stats output must be a packed BHSD tensor.` |
| `tests/attention/test_cudnn_graph_cache_key.py` | 1 | `ValueError: attn_scale with tensor and value cannot be set at the same time.` |

## Root cause

The CI image runs **frontend 1.28.0 against backend `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 9.24.0.43**. Frontend 1.28 enforces a constraint that 1.27 did not: below backend 9.26.0, a non-ragged Stats output must be packed BHSD.

FlashInfer declares the LSE/Stats tensor token-major, which is not packed BHSD — `flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py:586`:

```python
Stats.set_uid(UIDs.STATS_UID.value).set_output(
    return_lse
).set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT).set_dim(
    [graph_b, h_qo, graph_s_qo, 1]
).set_stride([graph_s_qo * h_qo, 1, h_qo, 1])   # b,s,h order -> not packed BHSD
```

The ragged path sets `Stats.set_ragged_offset(...)` just above and is exempt, which matches the failures landing only on the non-ragged path.

`requirements.txt` carries **no floor for the backend** (`nvidia-cudnn-cu12` comes in via torch), so #5131 moved the frontend forward while the backend stayed put, and the two are now on opposite sides of the 9.26.0 boundary.

## Evidence it is #5131

`JIT Unittest (H100)` on `main`, newest last:

| commit | H100 |
|---|---|
| `80342aea` | ✅ success — last green |
| `7c513848` | cancelled |
| **`01f19ab9` (#5131)** | cancelled |
| `65146a59`, `6268039d` | cancelled |
| `c05407ce` | ❌ failure (134 nodes) |

`c05407ce` is the first non-cancelled run after #5131, and it fails with exactly the nodes above.

## Note: this is not test-only

Any user on frontend ≥ 1.28 with backend < 9.26 who requests LSE on the non-ragged prefill path hits this. Worth deciding whether the pre-1.28 combination was silently producing a wrong LSE, or whether 1.28's check is stricter than the backend actually requires — that answer picks the fix.

## Possible remedies (not ranked)

1. Cap the frontend (`nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.27,<1.28`) to restore the last-known-green pair.
2. Add a backend floor (`nvidia-cudnn-cu12>=9.26.0`; 9.26.0.51 is released) so the constraint no longer applies.
3. Gate in code: extend the existing `_supports_*` version check in `flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py` so the non-ragged LSE path falls back when the backend is below 9.26.0.

## Environment

From the failing job ([103361522850](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/34629133585/job/103361522850)):

```
nvidia-cudnn-cu12         9.24.0.43
nvidia-cudnn-frontend     1.28.0
```
